optimizer: Claude (coding agent), acting as the prompt optimizer of docs/prompt_optimizer_plan.md; Steph delegated tuning rounds 1-2 on 2026-11-19

diagnosis.behaviour: Near the limit, the agent tries to finish in one round with large bundles; they break the 15% step limit (round wasted) or pass with the run's costliest step.
evidence: 20%, round 15: three candidates of 16-30 choices freeing ~58 MB (all that was left): +53.2%, +49.5%, +25.5%, all rejected
20%, round 19: three 9-choice candidates freeing ~40 MB (all that was left): +20.2%, +20.4%, +20.9%, all rejected
20%, round 20: kept a 21-choice candidate at +14.6%, the run's largest step; its rise per MB (3.57) was worse than most earlier kept steps
30%, round 27: 'making it the strongest single-step fitting alternative'; rounds 27-28 rejected at +19% to +28%
diagnosis.cause: The instructions never say that reaching the limit sooner is worth nothing, nor that choices applied together interact. Rounds were never short (20 of 40 used at 20%), so the rush has no reason.

diagnosis.behaviour: The agent re-proposes plans already measured; the code refuses them and the round is lost.
evidence: 30%, round 30: 'candidate 1 gives a plan already evaluated in an earlier round'
diagnosis.cause: The rules section the code fills in already says 'none may repeat a model already measured'; the agent did not follow it. Not an instructions gap.

diagnosis.behaviour: The agent picks layers to drop from the quick tests rather than the measured damage.
evidence: 20%, round 15: 'Quick tests identify layer 3 as an unusually low-damage drop candidate' (rejected at +53%)
diagnosis.cause: The instructions already say to use measured damage for the layer choice; one instance only, so not edited this round.

edits.with:
Candidates are your experiments: make them test different ideas, not small
variations of one idea. Small steps let you re-measure before committing
further. Choices in one candidate interact: together they often do more damage
than the sum of their separate measurements. Reaching the limit in fewer
rounds earns nothing; only perplexity at the limit counts. You can return to
an earlier kept plan, but a later step cannot undo the damage of an earlier
one.
edits.fixes: rushing to the limit with large bundles
edits.expected_signal: fewer candidates that free all remaining memory at once; fewer ROLLBACK rounds near the limit; a smaller final step (< +10%); lower unseen-validation perplexity at the same limit

not_instruction_issues: Quick tests are misleading for layer drops on this model (known since task 2.x); the instructions already rank measured damage above them for choosing layers.

Repeated plans (30% run, rounds 30-31) despite the rule being stated; the code already refuses them, costing one round each. If it recurs, the code could list the already-measured plans next to the rule.
neutrality_check: Neither edit names, ranks or discourages a method or a layer; both state facts true of the system (the validator refuses repeated plans; the score is perplexity at the limit; interaction is observed in the round results the agent sees).
